title: US Resumes Green Card Lottery Visa Issuance With September 30 Deadline Looming
excerpt: The State Department has resumed Diversity Visa processing after a federal court order ended a months-long suspension, giving applicants a narrow window before the fiscal year closes.
body:
• The U.S. State Department resumed Diversity Visa issuance on August 28, 2026, following a federal court order in Medani et al. v. Trump et al.
  • The program had been suspended since December 2025, when the Trump administration halted it citing national security concerns after attacks at Brown University and MIT.
  • DV-2026 winners face a hard September 30 deadline — unused visa numbers cannot be carried over to the next fiscal year.
  • Indians are generally not eligible for the Diversity Visa lottery due to India's high immigration levels to the US.

Court Order Ends Months-Long Freeze

The U.S. State Department confirmed that it resumed issuing Diversity Immigrant Visas on August 28, 2026, in compliance with a federal court order that ended a suspension lasting more than eight months. The development offers relief to thousands of DV-2026 lottery winners whose applications had been frozen since December 2025.

The resumption follows litigation in Medani et al. v. Trump et al., where a federal court certified three subclasses of DV-2026 applicants and preliminarily blocked three visa-freeze policies implemented by the Trump administration, finding them "likely to be arbitrary and capricious," according to immigration law firm BAL. A September 18 status conference has been scheduled to review the progress of adjudications.

Why the Program Was Suspended

The Department of Homeland Security, under Secretary Kristi Noem, ordered the suspension of the Diversity Visa Lottery Program on December 19, 2025, citing national security concerns. The move followed the December 18 attacks at Brown University and MIT, in which law enforcement identified the suspect as a Portuguese national who had entered the U.S. through the DV Program in 2017, according to Envoy Global.

The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services subsequently placed holds on all pending Form I-485 adjustment of status applications filed by Diversity Visa selectees, as well as related employment authorization, advance parole and waiver applications. USCIS also ordered interviews or re-interviews for DV applicants to reassess security concerns.

The September 30 Deadline

For DV-2026 winners, timing is critical. Diversity Visas are tied to the U.S. fiscal year and must be issued by September 30, 2026. If a visa number is not used by that date, it is permanently lost and cannot be carried over, according to immigration law firm Fragomen.

This means that simply being selected in the lottery does not guarantee a Green Card. Applicants must complete all required processing, satisfy eligibility requirements and receive their visa before the fiscal-year deadline. With barely a month remaining, the window for pending applicants is extremely tight.

"All selectees, including family members, must be issued visas by September 30, 2026. Under no circumstances can the Department of State issue DVs nor can USCIS approve adjustments after this date."

— U.S. State Department, DV-2026 Instructions

What It Means for Indians

Indians are generally not eligible for the Diversity Visa lottery. The program is designed for nationals of countries with historically low levels of immigration to the United States. Countries that have sent large numbers of immigrants through certain categories are excluded, and India falls into that group due to its high immigration volumes.

However, eligibility is primarily determined by country of birth, with limited exceptions. An Indian-born applicant who is a national of an eligible country through a spouse or parent may qualify in certain circumstances, according to the State Department's published guidelines.

What's Next

The Diversity Visa program makes up to 55,000 immigrant visas available annually to individuals selected randomly from eligible countries. Applicants who were selected for DV-2026 should check their status through the official Entrant Status Check portal at dvprogram.state.gov, using their confirmation number. The State Department has warned applicants to be vigilant against scams, noting it never makes selection notifications by mail, email or phone. For those eligible and selected, the immediate priority is ensuring their applications are fully processed before the September 30 cutoff.
